title: Understanding the Model
text: The model given is hat{y}_i=f_{theta}(x_i)=theta*e**(sqrt(abs(x_i))). This means that the prediction for each observation is based on the parameter theta and the exponential function of the square root of the absolute value of $$x_i$$.

title: Ordinary Least Squares (OLS)
text: OLS is a method used to estimate the parameters in a linear regression model by minimizing the sum of the squared differences between the observed and predicted values.

title: Sum of Residuals
text: The sum of residuals in a linear regression model is the sum of the differences between the observed values and the predicted values. In OLS, this sum is always zero.

title: Model Predictions
text: Consider the form of the model: hat{y}_i=theta*e**(sqrt(abs(x_i))). Since $$e^{\sqrt{|x_i|}}$$ is always positive, the sign of hat{y}_i depends on theta.

hintAnswer: We can use ordinary least squares (OLS) to estimate the optimal hat{theta}.
title: Applying OLS
text: Given the model hat{y}_i=theta*e**(sqrt(abs(x_i))), can we apply OLS to estimate theta?
choices: The sum of residuals of our model will always be $$0$$.
The predictions of our model can never be negative.
We can use ordinary least squares (OLS) to estimate the optimal hat{theta}.
